sights.address: Oracle Park (Giants ballpark), South of Market, San Francisco, CA 94107
sights.w: Bayfront home of the SF Giants — the Coca-Cola bottle slide, the giant glove, McCovey Cove splash hits and the ballpark crab sandwich.

sights.address: 425 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94105
sights.w: 5.4-acre rooftop park atop the Salesforce Transit Center — 600 trees, 16,000 plants, a linear fountain, a gondola and ~20 free events a week.

sights.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, SoMa, San Francisco, CA 94103
sights.w: Three city blocks of gardens, public art and free concerts; walk behind the falling-water curtain of the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial.

sights.address: Chase Center, Mission Bay, San Francisco, CA 94158
sights.w: The Warriors' arena (opened 2019) and concert venue; the surrounding Thrive City blocks carry restaurants and a bay-side plaza.

sights.address: Sutro Heights Park, above the Cliff House / Ocean Beach, San Francisco, CA 94121
sights.w: Adolph Sutro's 1885 hilltop garden above the Cliff House — the parapet, stone wall and statue plinths, with views over Ocean Beach. Free, part of the GGNRA.

sights.address: Lyon Street Steps, Lyon St (Pacific Heights–Cow Hollow, at the Presidio's Broadway Gate), San Francisco, CA 94123
sights.w: Nearly 300 hedge-lined steps linking Pacific Heights and Cow Hollow to the Presidio's Broadway Gate, with bay views. Free.

sights.address: Tank Hill Park, Twin Peaks Blvd / end of Belgrave Ave, San Francisco, CA 94117
sights.w: A 2.9-acre rocky knob in Ashbury Heights — the locals' quieter Twin Peaks, with a sweeping city panorama. Free.
sights.k: view hill park free hidden gem

sights.address: Seward Mini Park, Seward St / 70 Corwin St, San Francisco, CA 94114
sights.w: A pair of parallel concrete slides built into a Castro hillside mini-park — bring cardboard. Free.

sights.n: Blue Heron Lake (Stow Lake) & Strawberry Hill
sights.address: Blue Heron Lake (formerly Stow Lake), Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
sights.w: Golden Gate Park's largest man-made lake (renamed Blue Heron Lake) — a 1-mile loop, boat rentals and the 430-ft Strawberry Hill island with its waterfall. Free to walk.

sights.address: Crane Cove Park, Dogpatch waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94107
sights.w: Seven-acre Port park in Dogpatch on the old Union Iron Works shipyard — a small public beach for kayaks and paddleboards, the historic cranes, a big playground and grills. Free.

sights.address: Heron's Head Park, Bayview waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94124
sights.w: 22-acre restored wetland on a Bayview pier spit — shoreline trails thick with migratory birds and the off-grid EcoCenter. Free.

sights.address: Bayview Opera House, 3rd St, Bayview, San Francisco, CA 94124
sights.w: SF's oldest theater building (1888), survivor of the 1906 quake — now the Bayview's community arts hub.

sights.address: India Basin Shoreline Park, Bayview waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94124
sights.w: 10-acre Bayview waterfront park (opened 2024-25) — paths, food gardens, amphitheaters and a food pavilion for chef pop-ups. Free.

sights.address: Huntington Park, 1050 Taylor St, San Francisco, CA 94108
sights.w: 1.3-acre Nob Hill square between Grace Cathedral and the Fairmont, centred on its Fountain of the Tortoises. Free.

sights.address: 950 Mason St, San Francisco, CA 94108
sights.w: The 1907 grand hotel crowning Nob Hill, where the UN Charter was drafted in 1945 — lobby and view terraces open to all.

sights.address: Macondray Lane (stairs at Taylor St), Russian Hill, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: Leafy two-block pedestrian lane on Russian Hill — Armistead Maupin's model for Barbary Lane in Tales of the City. Free.

sights.address: Ina Coolbrith Park, Russian Hill, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: Tiny terraced Russian Hill park with a sweeping view over the Financial District and the Bay Bridge. Free.

sights.address: Haight St & Ashbury St, San Francisco, CA 94117
sights.w: The corner where 1960s flower power blossomed — Victorian hillsides, vintage and record shops along Upper Haight.

sights.address: Buena Vista Park, Haight-Ashbury, San Francisco, CA 94117
sights.w: SF's oldest official park (1867) — a wooded hill above the Haight with city and bay views. Free.

sights.address: Corona Heights Park (by the Randall Museum), San Francisco, CA 94114
sights.w: Red-chert rock outcrop above the Castro and the Haight with a 360-degree view (and the Randall Museum at its foot). Free.

sights.address: Fort Mason Center, Marina waterfront, San Francisco, CA 94123
sights.w: Former Army post turned waterfront arts and community campus between the Marina and Aquatic Park — piers, galleries, theatres and the Great Meadow. Free to wander.

sights.address: Crissy Field, Presidio, San Francisco, CA 94129
sights.w: Former military airfield turned restored tidal marsh and bayfront promenade, with the Golden Gate dead ahead. Free.

sights.address: Alta Plaza Park, Pacific Heights, San Francisco, CA 94115
sights.w: Terraced Pacific Heights hilltop park — from the top you see clear across the bay to Sausalito. Free.

sights.address: City Lights Bookstore, Columbus Ave at Jack Kerouac Alley, North Beach, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: Lawrence Ferlinghetti's 1953 bookstore and publisher — ground zero of the Beat movement, three floors of books and poetry.

sights.address: Washington Square, North Beach (facing Saints Peter and Paul Church), San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: North Beach's green heart under the twin spires of Saints Peter and Paul — morning tai chi, focaccia from the corner bakery. Free.

sights.address: Old St. Mary's Cathedral, California St, Chinatown, San Francisco, CA 94108
sights.w: California's first cathedral (1854), built of granite quarried in China and brick shipped round Cape Horn, at the edge of Chinatown.

sights.address: Ocean Beach, western edge of the Sunset/Richmond, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: Seven miles of wild Pacific sand on the city's western edge, from the Cliff House to Fort Funston — big surf, bonfire rings, sunsets. Free.

sights.address: Fort Funston, southwest San Francisco coast (GGNRA), San Francisco, CA
sights.w: Wind-scoured coastal bluffs where hang-gliders launch over the Pacific; sandy trails down to the beach. Free (GGNRA).

sights.address: San Francisco Zoo & Gardens, by Ocean Beach, Sunset District, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: Northern California's largest zoo, by Ocean Beach.

sights.address: Sigmund Stern Recreation Grove, Sunset District, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: 33-acre eucalyptus-and-redwood dell whose free summer Stern Grove Festival concerts draw throngs.

sights.address: Clarion Alley, between Mission & Valencia, 17th & 18th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
sights.w: The Clarion Alley Mural Project's open-air gallery — 700+ murals since 1992 on social, economic and environmental justice. Free.

sights.address: 3543 18th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
sights.w: Women-led community centre (1979) wrapped in the MaestraPeace mural honouring women leaders and artists worldwide.

sights.address: Harvey Milk Plaza, Market St / Castro St / 17th St, San Francisco, CA 94114
sights.w: Memorial plaza to Harvey Milk at the Castro's crossroads — under the giant rainbow flag, the entrance to Castro station.

sights.address: Mount Davidson Park, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: The city's highest natural point (928 ft) — a 1.5-mile forest loop to the historic Mount Davidson Cross.

sights.address: Glen Canyon Park, Glen Park, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: 70-acre wild canyon with rock outcrops and a creek in the middle of the city. Free.

sights.address: San Francisco City Hall, Van Ness Ave, Civic Center, San Francisco, CA 94102
sights.w: Beaux-Arts City Hall on Van Ness Avenue, the grand centrepiece of the Civic Center.

sights.address: Union Square, Downtown, San Francisco, CA 94108
sights.w: The 2.6-acre plaza at the heart of the shopping and hotel district, ringed by department stores. Free.

sights.address: Maiden Lane, off Union Square, San Francisco, CA 94108
sights.w: Pedestrian-only alley off Union Square — once a notorious red-light street, now boutiques and cocktail bars. Free.

sights.address: Lotta's Fountain, Market St / Geary St / Kearny St, San Francisco, CA 94103
sights.w: 1875 cast-iron fountain where survivors of the 1906 earthquake used to meet — said to be haunted by them still. Free.

sights.address: 2 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA 94105
sights.w: The 1875 Palace (rebuilt 1909 after the quake) — step into the Garden Court under 80,000 panes of stained glass.

sights.address: Old San Francisco Mint, SoMa, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: Greek Revival landmark (1874) that minted gold coins until 1937 — now used for exhibitions and events.

sights.address: Pioneer Park / Filbert Steps, Telegraph Hill, San Francisco, CA 94133
sights.w: A feral flock of cherry-headed conures (descended from escapees c.1990) wheeling over the Filbert Steps gardens below Coit Tower. Free.

sights.address: Japan Center (Kinokuniya, Japan Center West & East malls), Geary Blvd / Post St, Japantown, San Francisco, CA 94115
sights.w: The 1968 three-mall heart of the oldest Japantown in the US — Kinokuniya books, ramen and udon counters, beside the Peace Pagoda.

sights.address: 1805 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94115
sights.w: Historic 1912 music hall — the Fillmore Auditorium that hosted the Grateful Dead and James Brown, epicentre of 1960s psychedelic rock, and still a working venue.

sights.address: Haas-Lilienthal House, Pacific Heights, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: Authentic 1886 Queen Anne Victorian by architect Peter Schmidt, listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

sights.address: 1 Loraine Ct, San Francisco, CA 94118
sights.w: Neoclassical domed columbarium — the last remnant of the Richmond's Odd Fellows Cemetery — restored after decades of ruin, with a stained-glass dome over two balconied rings of niches.

sights.address: Bison Paddock, west of Spreckels Lake on John F. Kennedy Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA
sights.w: A small herd of American bison grazing in western Golden Gate Park — a city institution since 1892. Free.

sights.address: 1000 Great Highway, San Francisco, CA 94121
sights.w: 1925 seaside chalet at the foot of Golden Gate Park whose ground floor is wrapped in 1936-37 WPA fresco murals of everyday San Francisco.
